# C# Instructions

These instructions define the coding conventions for C# in this workspace.

## Language Version

C# / .NET 10.0 (nullable enabled, implicit usings enabled)

## Error Handling

- Throw typed exceptions; never swallow exceptions silently
- Catch and translate at controller boundaries
- v2 controllers MUST return `ApiResponse<T>` (never raw data) with correlation ID and proper HTTP status (200 / 400 / 401 / 500)
- v1 controllers use the legacy `ServiceResponse` wrapper for backward compatibility
- Log errors via `LogHelper`; never `Console.WriteLine` in production paths

## Naming Conventions

- PascalCase for types, methods, properties, public fields, namespaces
- camelCase for locals, parameters, and private fields (`_camelCase` allowed for private fields)
- Interfaces prefixed with `I` (e.g., `IResourceTypeService`)
- Async methods suffixed with `Async`
- File names match the public type they declare

## Code Organization

- Layered architecture: Controllers → Services → Repositories → Storage (JSON / SQLite)
- Each service has a matching interface in `Services/Interfaces/IXxxService.cs` and is registered scoped (per-request) in `Program.cs`
- v2 controllers go under `Controllers/V2/` and return `ApiResponse<T>` with correlation IDs
- Razor components: pages in `Components/Pages/`, modals in `Components/Modals/`, shared in `Components/General/` and `Components/Layout/`
- Default seed data in `src/repository/`; runtime config in `src/settings/` (copied on first run)
- ADRs go in `docs/v5.0.0/adrs/`

## Documentation

- XML doc comments (`/// <summary>...</summary>`) on all public types and members
- Inline `<remarks>` for non-obvious behavior; `<exception>` for thrown exception types
- Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) under `docs/v5.0.0/adrs/`
- README and migration guides under `docs/v5.0.0/`

## Testing

- Tests live in `tests/AzureNamingTool.UnitTests/` (xunit + Moq + FluentAssertions)
- UI tests live in `tests/AzureNamingTool.UiTests/` (Playwright + LightBDD + NUnit, targets net8.0)
- Test class name mirrors the system-under-test class name (`MyServiceTests`)
- AAA pattern: Arrange / Act / Assert — comments optional but encouraged for non-trivial cases
- Use `Moq` for service collaborators; `FluentAssertions` for readable expectations
- Run a single test with: `dotnet test --filter "FullyQualifiedName~MyTestClass.MyTestMethod"`

## Dependencies

- Manage NuGet packages in `src/AzureNamingTool.csproj`
- Prefer `Microsoft.*` and well-established community packages
- Pin to compatible major versions; avoid floating wildcards in production builds
- New transitive dependencies require ADR justification when added for runtime use

## Safety & Security

- `<Nullable>enable</Nullable>` is on; respect nullability annotations
- No `unsafe` code blocks
- No reflection-based bypasses of typing or DI
- All file-system access MUST resolve within the workspace; reject path traversal
- API key validation runs before any authorized action

## Performance

- Prefer `async`/`await` for I/O; never block on `.Result` or `.Wait()`
- Use `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` for streaming results when applicable
- Cache configuration data via `CacheHelper` to avoid repeated JSON/SQLite reads
- Avoid LINQ-to-Entities materializing large lists when a count or projection suffices

## Anti-Patterns

The following patterns are prohibited:

- Direct file or SQLite access from services — go through `IConfigurationRepository<T>` / `IStorageProvider`
- Returning raw data from v2 controllers — always wrap in `ApiResponse<T>`
- Hard-coding paths — use `appsettings.json` and `ConfigurationHelper`
- Skipping `[ApiKey]` on new API endpoints
- Catching `Exception` then re-throwing without context loss preservation
